charts.units: percent of wasted food; US short tons

source.title: EPA, 2019 Wasted Food Report, corrected April 2024
source.method: Direct transcription of published management rows and percentages.

limits: Food retail, food service, and residential sectors only; manufacturing is excluded.
Wasted food includes inedible parts, not a quantity that could all be donated.
Donation excludes food banks' undistributed portion, which is assigned to other pathways.
Published integer rows sum to one ton above the published total; retained as transcribed. Percentages sum to 100.00.

source.title: USDA NASS, Land Values 2026 Summary
source.locator: Average Farm Real Estate Value, printed page 5, PDF page 5
source.method: All 15 labeled annual values transcribed from the published chart.

limits: Includes farm land and buildings; not vacant land alone.
Nominal, not inflation-adjusted; national averages are not local asking prices.

charts.units: percent of households food insecure at some time in 2024

source.title: USDA ERS, Household Food Security in the United States in 2024, ERR-358
source.locator: Table 2, printed page 20, PDF page 26; discussion printed page 18
source.method: Selected non-overlapping income groups, not all income categories.

limits: Selected groups omit middle incomes and unknown income.
National rate covers all households, not just the two shown.
Survey association does not establish causation; food insecurity is not identical to reduced intake for every member.

source.title: IEA, Key Questions on Energy and AI (2026)
source.locator: Our updated data centre electricity demand outlook
source.method: Two stated values only; no intermediate or extrapolated points.

limits: All data centres worldwide, not AI-only electricity.
The 2030 figure is a projection, not an observation.

charts.units: calendar year at 50 percent aggregate forecast probability

source.title: Grace et al., Thousands of AI Authors on the Future of AI
source.method: Four aggregate forecast dates, also present in canonical Chapter 1 Table 3.

limits: These are aggregate probabilistic forecasts from respondents, not actual arrival dates, guarantees, or observed technology progress.
High-level machine intelligence and full labor automation are different milestones.

charts.units: gigajoules per tonne of ammonia, net basis

source.title: IEA, Ammonia Technology Roadmap (2021)
source.locator: Paragraph beginning: Using technology to improve the performance of existing equipment
source.method: Global-average estimate and two best-available-technology benchmarks.

limits: 2021 report values, not a current census of plants.
Benchmarks are not proof every existing plant can reach them, or that biological fixation has no energy cost.

charts.units: decimal gigabytes of nominal model weights only

source.title: Canonical Chapter 11, The memory math
source.locator: Chapter equation with overhead factor omitted for this weights-only comparison; server documentation explains context and memory options.

limits: Not measured VRAM demand or a hardware purchasing specification.
Excludes quantization metadata, KV cache, activations, runtime buffers, and simultaneous users.
The chapter's illustrative 20 percent allowance is not included here.

source.title: Canonical Chapter 18, Put the failed meal on the board
source.locator: Six-row premortem record and the following handoff-test instruction.

rows.question: WHAT WARNS YOU?
rows.detail: Define a signal or missing check-in.

rows.question: WHO RESPONDS?
rows.detail: Confirm a lead and an available backup.

rows.question: WHAT GETS DELIVERED?
rows.detail: Test the alternative; show any gap.

rows.question: WHAT KEEPS IT RUNNING?
rows.detail: Name supplies, labor, money, end date.

rows.question: WHEN DO YOU CHECK AGAIN?
rows.detail: Set a review date and needed evidence.

limits: Illustrative worksheet, not results from an actual service or a measured risk model.
Personal details belong in appropriate private records, not the public board.
